title: Laos suspends fuel-powered vehicle imports in drive to accelerate EV adoption
content: Laos temporarily bans imports of petrol and diesel vehicles from June 1, 2026 through end-2026 to accelerate EV adoption and cut fossil-fuel dependence. Fully electric vehicles under USD 50,000 are exempt from excise tax, and the Ministry of Industry and Commerce is instructed to set a standardised EV pricing structure (price control). Supports the national goal of EVs exceeding 30 percent of vehicles on roads by 2030.

title: Laos Orders Civil Servants to Work From Home, Switch to Electric Vehicles Amid Fuel Crisis
content: PM Sonexay Siphandone issued an emergency decree to cut fuel use via remote work and vehicle electrification: 30 percent cut in EV registration fees, streamlined EV import procedures, and a requirement that transport companies keep at least 10 percent EVs in fleets by end-2026. Response to severe fuel shortages (diesel prices up ~50 percent in early March).

title: Lao government unveils EV target and new policies
content: Laos set EV adoption targets of 1 percent by 2025 and over 30 percent by 2030, leading via state administration vehicles and encouraging state enterprises and public transport to switch to EVs. Incentives include 0 percent import tariff, 3 percent consumption tax, 10 percent VAT, excise exemption for EVs under USD 50,000, and a 30 percent annual road-tax reduction vs petrol equivalents.
